gaps.why_now: A dedicated Phase 11 build entry now keeps the landed gpio_wdt starter and the survey checkpoint reviewable together instead of letting the lane drift after the first driver scaffold landed.
The survey gate now acts as a freshness check around the landed gpio_wdt starter so the lane does not drift back to pre-driver assumptions or overclaim broader watchdog progress.
The survey note now records the landed gpio_wdt starter and the new probe-summary follow-up so the remaining Phase 11 gap stays explicit without overclaiming broader watchdog progress.

The first gpio_wdt starter is now landed and models hw_algo parsing, heartbeat margin validation, bounded start or stop or ping transitions, and a tiny probe-time summary without touching live GPIO or platform registration.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep the toggle and level state transitions, heartbeat validation, always-running stop behavior, and pre-registration probe bookkeeping honest around the landed simple-driver scaffold.
A bounded slice note records exactly what the gpio_wdt starter and probe-summary helper cover so later Phase 11 work can extend the model without reopening the starter contract.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary for always-running startup, requested GPIO line mode, and watchdog-core-facing bookkeeping so the starter describes more of gpio_wdt_probe() before any live GPIO or platform glue.
The next honest gpio_wdt step is a tiny nowayout-aware follow-up so the starter can distinguish watchdog-core stop gating from hardware always-running semantics before any live GPIO or platform glue.

Platform-driver registration, GPIO descriptor acquisition, watchdog core registration, and reboot integration remain blocked until the lane grows a slightly richer probe model and a hardware-validation plan.
